Screenshot of a browser showing a local file, pondmap/grid.html: a dark, neon-cyan network map titled “PONDSIDE · THE GRID.” The header reads “Thu, Oct 15 at 11:05 AM · 27 Incus · 12 Docker · 7 agents on the LAN · mock,” above a row of filter tabs (All, Agents, Infra, Services, LAN Devices and others).

At the top, two boxes connect by glowing lines down into the LAN: “On the tailnet” (iphone-15-pro, iphone101, macbook-air) and “The internet” (upstream-color). Below, a large “Apartment LAN” panel (192.168.0.0/24, TP-Link router does DHCP) contains “PRIMER,” captioned “The whole town. Every container below lives in this one box.”

Inside Primer, the br0 bridge holds a grid of 24 container chips. Eight are orange: automat, beaker, claudewatch, credible-labrador (struck through), dr-know, hellonurse, joan and mr-d3w3y. The other 16 are cyan, including archive, chalkboard, comfyui, cortex, homeassistant, runpod, smithy and zenit, which is selected and glowing white.

Smaller dashed boxes show other networks: incusbr0 (br4dbury, mrs-johnson), incusbr1 (bsl-4), firecrawl_backend (api, nuq-postgres, playwright-service, rabbitmq, redis, searxng, tailscale), several Docker networks, two empty bridges, and Primer’s own interfaces. An “Everything else on the LAN” box lists 22 devices by manufacturer, mostly Espressif.

A detail panel on the right describes zenit: Incus container, infra, on br0, “Telegram bot and metrics.” It notes a global IPv6 address with inbound traffic left to the router’s firewall, and lists status Running, IPv4 192.168.0.157, an Ubuntu noble image, a zenit-data disk mounted at /data, and tailnet online.
